mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -18.0 to -10.9 over the three weeks before the decision point; this momentum continues as activity normalizes, lifting the next 28-day mean above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly means rose from -18.0 to -10.9 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, meaning the three-week improvement does not carry forward.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility is above 60 percent above baseline, outdoor leisure competes with indoor discretionary shopping; because PARKS remains elevated at 58.4 after peaking at 70.1, retail trips are diverted and RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above 60 percent above baseline for at least one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 70.1 and 58.4 in t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than over the last 14 days while PARKS remains above 60 percent above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals restored commuting and office presence, increasing weekday retail footfall; if TRANSIT improves by at least 2 points and WORKPLACES by at least 3 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 2 points and WORKPLACES by more than 3 points versus the prior week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -27.0 to -26.7 and WORKPLACES from -21.4 to -17.6 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: When the joint improvement threshold is met, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, falling RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are spending more time outside the home; because RESIDENTIAL dropped from 5.3 to 2.7 in the latest week, discretionary retail trips increase over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1 point week-on-week while remaining positive.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 5.3 to 2.7 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines by at least 1 point but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than or equal to the last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility above 7 percent above baseline signals continued precautionary shopping and limited discretionary trips; if GROCERY_PHARM remains at or above 7, RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks as consumers stay cautious.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is at or above 7 percent above baseline.
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM is at or above 7, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS from 70.1 to 58.4 marks the end of a peak outdoor-activity week; as outdoor trips normalize, some time and spending shifts back to retail, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 8 points week-on-week from a level above 60.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 70.1 to 58.4 between t-1w and t-0w
regime_hint: late spring to early summer transition
failure_condition: After a PARKS drop of more than 8 points from above 60, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than or equal to the last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Policy-driven transit avoidance, visible as TRANSIT below -25, suppresses non-essential retail trips; only if TRANSIT recovers above -25 while GROCERY_PHARM stays below 6 do retail-and-recreation visits increase over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -25 and GROCERY_PHARM falls below 6.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remains below -25 and GROCERY_PHARM is 8.0 in t-0w
failure_condition: When TRANSIT rises above -25 and GROCERY_PHARM falls below 6, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The latest WORKPLACES rebound from -21.4 to -17.6 signals a short-run return of commuting and office-adjacent spending; this lifts RETAIL_REC within one week even if the broader level remains below baseline.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points week-on-week from a level below -20.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -21.4 to -17.6 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: Following a WORKPLACES rise of at least 3 points from below -20, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than or equal to the last 7-day mean.
